- Q1. For `https://docs.stripe.com/payments/wechat-pay/accept-a-payment`, what documented behavior, prerequisites, actors and state transitions does the complete new capture establish? How do these compare with the matched prior capture and each mapped summary?

- Q2. Which changes are substantive, presentational or navigation-only? Identify the exact dated qualifications, conflicts and reciprocal routes that the proposed disposition should preserve.

reviewed_answers.Q1: The full 2026-11-07 capture at https://docs.stripe.com/payments/wechat-pay/accept-a-payment lists Checkout, Direct API, iOS and Android in new raw lines 9-16, without additional behavior. Old raw lines 8-319 from 2026-05-08 describe one-time same-currency Checkout or a merchant-server PaymentIntent with a client secret for direct Stripe.js confirmation. For May web Direct API, the merchant renders the returned QR, the customer authenticates in WeChat, and the server uses Stripe events to distinguish succeeded from failure with requires_payment_method. Sandbox simulations are separate. source-stripe-wechat-pay-accept-payment.md retains the central historical behavior but overstates web-only applicability and the count of eligible Checkout country codes.
reviewed_answers.Q2: At https://docs.stripe.com/payments/wechat-pay/accept-a-payment, new raw lines 9-16 replace the presentation of the full dated old raw lines 8-319 with four navigation links. New iOS and Android routes do not establish when support changed or what those SDKs do. Preserve May's one-time Checkout modes, webhook outcome boundary and 35 listed business codes against the distinct 22-location overview. Preserve the separate November eligible-native description alongside its Mobile Payment Element constraint and the exact Stripe.js mobile_web declaration as its own web contract. Date manual PaymentIntent writes and preserve both integration captures in source-stripe-wechat-pay-accept-payment.md with reciprocal Stripe index and Wallets concept routes and its distinct method overview.
